items: Securing ML code and containers today
Reverse mindmap: when the question points here

CodeGuru Reviewer analyzes Java and Python repositories with program analysis and machine learning, and comments on pull requests with suggestions on defects, resource leaks, security issues, and hard-coded secrets.

CodeGuru Profiler collects runtime data from live applications on JVM languages and Python and shows the most expensive lines of code, CPU bottlenecks, and latencyLatencyThe time between sending a request and receiving the response, usually measured in milliseconds. Distance and processing add to it; caching and serving users from nearby locations reduce it.Glossary entryClose problems, with recommendations.

Reviewer: repository associations (CodeCommit, GitHub, Bitbucket, and others), incremental reviews on pull requests, full repository scans, a detector library, and secrets detection that suggests moving secrets to AWS Secrets Manager.
Profiler: an agent in the application (on EC2, containers, or Lambda) sends profiles; flame graphs show where CPU time goes; anomaly and recommendation reports point to costly code paths.
Automated review comments on pull requests→ leads to CodeGuru Reviewer (no new associations since 2025-11-07)
Find the most CPU-expensive code at run time→ leads to CodeGuru Profiler
Scan container images for CVEs→ leads to Amazon Inspector
Keep secrets out of code→ leads to Secrets Manager
CodeGuru Reviewer reviews Java and Python code and finds secrets; since November 7, 2025, no new repository associations can be created.
CodeGuru Profiler finds expensive code and CPU bottlenecks in running JVM and Python applications.
To secure ML CI/CD pipelines in new designs, scan images and code with Amazon Inspector, control dependencies with CodeArtifact, and store secrets in Secrets Manager.

Amazon CodeGuru is a family of MLML (Machine learning)Software that learns patterns from example data to make predictions or decisions, instead of following rules written by hand. A model is first trained on data, then used to make predictions on new data, which is called inference.Glossary entryClose-powered developer tools that find problems in code:

Availability: since November 7, 2025, you can't create new repository associations in CodeGuru Reviewer; AWS documents other services with similar capabilities. Exam questions may still name CodeGuru for checking code in CI/CDCI/CD (Continuous integration and continuous delivery)Practices in which every code change is built and tested automatically (continuous integration) and kept ready to release, often deploying it automatically through a pipeline (continuous delivery or deployment).Glossary entryClose pipelines (MLA-C02 task 4.3.1), but new designs should use the alternatives below.
IAM controls access; code analyzed by Reviewer and profiling data are encrypted; repository access uses connections rather than stored credentials.
Managed services; Profiler's agent sends data asynchronously so it doesn't affect the application's availability.
Profiler's sampling has a low overhead and points to where optimization pays most, which also cuts compute cost.
Reviewer was priced by the lines of code analyzed; Profiler by sampling hours of the profiled application.

Recommendations appear in the console and in pull requests; Profiler reports anomalies; CloudTrail records APIAPI (Application programming interface)A defined way for one program to ask another for data or actions, such as a set of HTTPS requests and responses. Every AWS service is controlled through its API, which the console, the CLI, and the SDKs call for you.Glossary entryClose calls.
